title: Systemd Unit State Monitoring
exclusions: Compares an explicit, governed inventory of system-manager units with fresh, complete snapshots of documented systemd properties on the corresponding Linux hosts. It does not infer desired state from whichever units happen to be loaded; monitor user-manager units, containers that do not expose the host system manager, non-systemd init systems, or units absent from the exact policy; parse localized `systemctl status` text; prove that an active service is functionally healthy or serving correct responses; prove that a successful oneshot achieved its business outcome; or replace application, socket, timer, path, mount, dependency, journal, process, port, or transaction monitoring. `ActiveState`, `SubState`, `LoadState`, `UnitFileState`, `Result`, and `NRestarts` answer different questions. Unit-file enablement is not runtime state, an inactive oneshot can be healthy, and an active unit can still be degraded. Automatic-restart deltas are sampled observations, not counts of every manual start or process crash. Snapshot absence or incompleteness is observer health, not evidence that a unit stopped. The use case performs no start, stop, restart, enable, disable, mask, daemon-reload, reset-failed, remediation, security attribution, or regulatory attestation.
evidence: After deployment, retain the version-controlled `linux_systemd_unit_state_monitoring` saved-search definition and ACL, schedule and triggered-result history; the exact revision of `linux_systemd_unit_policy.csv`; the generated per-host `systemd-unit-targets.json` files and their `scope_version`/SHA-256 values; the reviewed `TA-linux-systemd-unit-state` collector hash and effective `inputs.conf`/`props.conf`; raw `unit_state` and `snapshot_complete` events; expected-host/unit coverage and collector-health reports; result exports; dispositions; and dated positive/negative control output. Each finding should preserve host, exact unit, desired load/active/sub/unit-file sets, observed `LoadState`/`ActiveState`/`SubState`/`UnitFileState`, service `Type`/`Result`/main-exit context, `NRestarts` and delta, boot/snapshot/scope identities, sample and state-change ages, owner, tier, and finding. During triage attach bounded same-time `systemctl show` output, relevant unit journal, effective unit/drop-ins, dependency and application checks before changing state. These artifacts show policy and sampled manager properties; this documentation-only review created no runtime evidence and does not prove continuous availability or successful service delivery.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated index and policy lookup, create fresh schema-1 snapshots for `unit-positive` with one previous and one latest complete snapshot, each declaring and indexing exactly two `unit_state` rows. Policy expects `api.service` to be `loaded|active|running`, permits unit-file state `enabled`, checks service result, and permits at most two automatic restarts per sample gap; the latest observation is `loaded|active|running`, `Result=success`, and changes `NRestarts` from 3 to 6. Policy also expects `missing.timer` as `loaded|active|waiting`, but that unit is not in either complete collector scope. Expect exactly two rows: `restart_delta_exceeded` for `api.service` with delta 3 and `unit_not_observed_in_complete_snapshot` for `missing.timer`. For host `unit-failed`, provide a latest `snapshot_complete` whose declared count is two but index only one unit row; expect `collector_latest_snapshot_incomplete`, and no runtime-state assertion based on its older complete snapshot.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Provide a fresh, count-complete snapshot for `unit-negative` after boot and transition grace. Policy expects long-running `sshd.service` as `loaded|active|running` with unit-file state `enabled`, and observes exactly those values with `Result=success`; its `NRestarts` rises from 4 to 6 against an allowed delta of two. Policy separately expects `backup.service`, a successful `Type=oneshot` without `RemainAfterExit`, as `loaded|inactive|dead`, permits unit-file state `static`, and checks `Result=success`. Add `updates.timer` expected and observed as `loaded|active|waiting` while its unit-file state policy is `ignore`. Keep collector scope versions equal, policy rows unique/unexpired, and latest sample age exactly 600 seconds. Expect zero results: the restart boundary is inclusive, inactive/dead is desired for this oneshot, ignored unit-file state is not compared, and freshness at the documented boundary remains accepted.

dataSources: Primary source: a locally maintained Universal Forwarder scripted input emits newline-delimited JSON every 60 seconds to deployment conventions `index=os`, `source=linux_systemd_unit_state`, and `sourcetype=linux:systemd:unit`. It reads an exact host-side collection scope and calls machine-oriented `systemctl show UNIT` for documented unit and service properties. Every `unit_state` row contains `record_type`, `collector_schema`, `snapshot_id`, `sample_epoch`, `sample_monotonic_usec`, `boot_id`, `boot_uptime_seconds`, `scope_version`, `scope_sha256`, exact `unit`, `query_status`, `query_return_code`, `LoadState`, `ActiveState`, `SubState`, `FreezerState`, `UnitFileState`, `UnitFilePreset`, `NeedDaemonReload`, condition/assert results, state-transition monotonic timestamps, invocation ID, fragment/source paths, and—where exposed by a service—`Type`, `Result`, `MainPID`, `ExecMainCode`, `ExecMainStatus`, `NRestarts`, and `Restart`. A terminal `snapshot_complete` declares unit count, collector status, and query-error count; SPL rejects snapshots whose indexed row count differs. Desired state comes separately from governed `linux_systemd_unit_policy.csv`, keyed by exact `host,unit`, with monitoring flag, matching `scope_version`, allowed load/active/sub/unit-file states, service-result check, restart-delta threshold, boot/transition grace, owner, service tier, and expiry. Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux `service.sh` (`sourcetype=Unix:Service`) is optional corroboration, not the primary contract. All custom names and fields are local conventions.
app: A customer-managed Universal Forwarder deployment app named `TA-linux-systemd-unit-state` supplies the reviewed Python collector, generated collection-scope JSON, scripted input, JSON source-type configuration, policy lookup, saved search, and dashboards; no premium Splunk app is required. Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (`Splunk_TA_nix`, Splunkbase 833) is optional for adjacent `service.sh` inventory and host context, but its stock `Unix:Service` event does not provide this snapshot-completeness, desired-state, freshness, restart-delta, and policy-expiry contract.

description: Identifies observer, policy, runtime-state, unit-file-state, service-result, daemon-reload, or restart-delta defects by reconciling every governed host/unit pair with the newest count-complete custom systemd snapshot. Desired load, active, sub, and enablement states are explicit policy; they are never inferred from observed inventory, and stale or incomplete collection cannot be reported as a stopped unit.
value: Critical services, timers, sockets, and other units can be missing, failed, disabled, flapping, or observed through a broken collector while the host itself remains reachable. A policy-left join improves triage by exposing completely absent units and telemetry gaps, respecting legitimate states such as successful inactive oneshots and static units, and giving operators exact manager properties and counter lifetimes without equating “active” with application health.
implementation: Generate one authoritative expected-unit policy and matching host collection scopes through configuration management, deploy the reviewed 60-second JSON scripted input, and validate every property against same-time `systemctl show`. Keep runtime (`LoadState`, `ActiveState`, `SubState`), installation (`UnitFileState`), service outcome (`Result`/exit fields), and restart-delta policy separate. Save the SPL as `linux_systemd_unit_state_monitoring`, schedule it every five minutes with the embedded two-minute indexing delay, and route collector/policy defects independently from unit-state findings. Never auto-restart a unit or infer health from an absent snapshot.
visualization: Use separate dashboard rows for `collector/policy`, `runtime`, `installation/configuration`, and `restart/outcome` findings so an absent snapshot is never shown as a stopped service. The primary latest-first table should include severity, host, unit, finding, owner/tier, desired versus observed load-active-sub state, desired versus observed unit-file state, service type/result/main exit context, restart delta/threshold, scope versions, snapshot age, and alert key. Add tiles for missing/stale/incomplete snapshots, duplicate/expired policy, unobserved units, failed/not-found units, daemon-reload needs, and restart bursts; a 24-hour state/finding trend; and an expected-versus-observed coverage matrix by host role. Drill down to the two raw snapshots, exact policy row, bounded unit journal, `systemctl show`, effective unit/drop-ins, dependencies, and application checks. Do not sum cumulative `NRestarts`, treat `inactive` alone as failure, merge desired and observed inventories, or show missing telemetry as a green host.
schema: Custom complete-snapshot systemd unit-property contract with separate desired-state policy; optional Unix:Service/Endpoint context is not equivalent
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable to the base rule. The Splunk Add-on's `Unix:Service` source type can map service inventory to the Endpoint data model, but no documented accelerated CIM dataset preserves exact expected host/unit policy, snapshot identity and declared count, observer freshness, systemd load/active/sub/unit-file/result semantics, monotonic transition age, boot-scoped `NRestarts` deltas, and scope-version agreement. A purpose-built summary may be used only if it retains every listed contract field and missing-entity behavior.

knownFalsePositives:
Every base result is a real mismatch, source-health defect, or sampled counter condition under the configured contracts. “False positive” normally means desired policy is wrong for the unit's type/lifecycle, the condition was approved, or identity/scope drift made two correct facts fail to join.

1. **Successful oneshot completion** — A `Type=oneshot` service without `RemainAfterExit=yes` normally becomes `inactive/dead` after status-zero completion. Model that exact unit as desired `inactive|dead` with `check_service_result=true`; do not globally require every `.service` unit to remain active or suppress all inactive services.

2. **Socket, timer, path, automount, and target activation semantics** — A healthy socket can be `active/listening`, a timer `active/waiting`, a path `active/waiting`, and a target `active/active`; their triggered services can be inactive between work. Set per-unit allowed states from same-time `systemctl show` and vendor design. Do not copy `running` from a long-lived service to every unit type.

3. **Boot, deployment, reload, or controlled restart transition** — Units can legitimately pass through activating, reloading, deactivating, auto-restart, and dead states during an approved boot or change. Use measured, short per-policy boot and state-change grace values and correlate the exact change/deployment and invocation. Never use a day-long grace or hide `not-found`, stale collection, failed result, or incomplete snapshot behind maintenance.

4. **Condition- or assertion-skipped unit** — A packaged service may intentionally remain inactive when `ConditionACPower`, path, virtualization, architecture, credential, or another unit condition is unmet. Compare `ConditionResult`/`AssertResult`, effective unit, host role, and vendor expectation. If skipping is desired, encode that unit/host policy; do not treat every false condition as healthy or every inactive state as failure.

5. **Static, indirect, generated, transient, template, or alias unit** — `UnitFileState=static` can be normal when a unit has no install section; generated/transient units and template instances have different installation lifecycles, and aliases can return a canonical `Id`. Use the exact canonical unit expected on that host and either list valid unit-file states or explicitly set `ignore`. Never infer runtime availability from `enabled` or suppress a `LoadState=not-found` merely because a similarly named alias exists.

6. **Approved mask, disablement, role retirement, or failover** — Maintenance or decommissioning may intentionally stop, disable, or mask one unit while another node serves traffic. Require exact host/unit, owner, change/failover evidence, bounded UTC interval, and post-change policy update. Desired inventory must change through governance; deleting a policy row just to clear an alert destroys missing-unit coverage.

7. **Automatic-restart counter lifetime or sampling gap** — `NRestarts` represents systemd's automatic restart counter, not every manual start. Reboot, manager/unit lifecycle changes, or counter reset can decrease it; the SPL groups by boot ID and reports only nonnegative consecutive deltas. A long sample gap can combine several legitimate restarts. Compare invocation IDs, unit journal, policy and deployment; preserve the burst even when recovery succeeded.

8. **Host identity, scope-version, or lookup drift** — Short name versus FQDN, cloned host metadata, stale configuration-management rollout, duplicate policy rows, or a target file generated from a different revision can create missing-unit or scope findings. Compare canonical Splunk `host`, boot ID, scope hash/version, deployment assignment, and lookup revision. Correct identity/configuration; do not add wildcard host aliases in the detection.

9. **Collector privilege, namespace, or bus failure** — A containerized or restricted forwarder can query a different manager or fail to connect while the host unit remains healthy. That is a collector/query finding, not a stopped unit. Run the exact read-only command as the collector identity in the host namespace, correct deployment, and avoid granting unrestricted sudo or the ability to change units.

**Safe notification suppression:** leave the base SPL, raw snapshots, and policy/collector findings intact. If local policy permits notification suppression, apply a post-result lookup such as `linux_systemd_unit_exceptions.csv` keyed by exact `host,unit,finding`, with `valid_from_epoch`, `valid_until_epoch`, `owner`, `approver`, `ticket`, and `reason`. Require bounded UTC validity and suppress only alert actions while preserving a review report. Reject host/unit wildcards, open-ended rows, exceptions for all collector or policy defects, and suppression of `unit_not_observed_in_complete_snapshot` without an approved policy change.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and semantic contract

Use this implementation only for the host system manager on Linux systems booted with systemd. Assign a platform owner for each unit, a configuration-management owner for desired inventory, a Splunk collection/content owner, and an incident path for each service tier. The Universal Forwarder identity needs permission to execute the packaged Python collector and read systemd properties over the local manager interface; it does not need permission to start, stop, enable, mask, reload, or edit units. Test the exact identity and namespace on every supported distribution and hardening profile. A forwarder in a container, user manager, or alternate mount/PID namespace is not automatically observing the host manager.

Define the meanings before collection. `LoadState` says whether the unit definition was loaded and can report states such as `loaded`, `not-found`, `bad-setting`, `error`, or `masked`. `ActiveState` is the high-level runtime state; `SubState` is unit-type-specific detail. `UnitFileState` describes installation/enablement and is not runtime. A static service can run, an enabled unit can fail, and a disabled unit can be started by dependency or manually. Service `Result`, `ExecMainCode`, and `ExecMainStatus` describe the most recent service execution outcome; they are not application probes. `NRestarts` counts automatic restarts exposed by the service manager and is compared only between consecutive complete samples within one boot. `NeedDaemonReload=yes` reports that the manager's loaded unit configuration differs from disk and does not itself say that runtime is failed.

Desired state must be authored separately. Never use `systemctl list-units`, a prior snapshot, or currently loaded units as the expected inventory: doing so makes a completely absent unit disappear from both sides. The policy lookup is the left side of the search. The collector target file is only the set of names to query. Generate both from one configuration-management source and give every revision a `scope_version`, but retain the independent policy because “what should exist and run” is not an observed systemd property.

The catalogue index, source, source type, app, lookup, 60-second interval, 600-second freshness threshold, two-minute indexing delay, and restart thresholds are deployment conventions. Measure and approve them. No Splunk version is claimed as runtime-validated, no premium app is required, and `status` remains draft until local acceptance and SME review are complete.

## Step 1 — Author desired inventory and collection scope

Create `linux_systemd_unit_policy.csv` with exactly one active row per canonical `host,unit`. Required columns are `host,unit,monitor,scope_version,desired_load_states,desired_active_states,allowed_sub_states,desired_unit_file_states,check_service_result,max_restart_delta,grace_after_boot_seconds,grace_after_state_change_seconds,owner,service_tier,valid_until_epoch`. Use lower-case pipe-delimited state tokens, for example `loaded`, `active`, `running`, and `enabled|enabled-runtime`. Set `desired_unit_file_states=ignore` only after consciously deciding installation state is irrelevant; this is often appropriate for generated, transient, or some template instances, not a shortcut for unknown policy. Use exact case-sensitive unit names even though this SPL normalizes host names.

Model each unit type. A long-running service commonly expects `loaded/active/running`. A successful oneshot without `RemainAfterExit=yes` commonly expects `loaded/inactive/dead` and `Result=success`. A timer commonly expects `active/waiting`; a socket commonly expects `active/listening`; actual substate tokens and unit-file states must be verified on the supported release and effective unit. Do not assume these examples fit vendor overrides. Inspect `systemctl show UNIT` and `systemctl cat UNIT`, read the package/vendor unit design, and write desired state that reflects the approved host role.

`check_service_result=true` is for service units where a non-success last result is actionable; use false for non-service units or where outcome has a separately defined contract. `max_restart_delta` is optional: leave it empty to disable restart-rate findings, or provide a nonnegative maximum automatic-restart increase allowed between normal 60-second samples. Two means deltas 0, 1, and 2 are accepted and 3 fires. It is not a per-hour threshold. If policy is hourly, redesign the SPL to aggregate complete samples over that hour and test counter resets rather than relabeling this delta.

Set `grace_after_boot_seconds` and `grace_after_state_change_seconds` from measured startup/reload behavior. Keep them short and unit-specific. They suppress only state comparisons; collector, policy, scope, query, daemon-reload, result, and restart evidence remain visible. Set an owner, one of critical/high/medium/low tiers, and a bounded policy expiry. Audit duplicate, missing, expired, and invalid rows before production.

Generate `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/TA-linux-systemd-unit-state/local/systemd-unit-targets.json` on each host, for example:

```json
{"schema_version":1,"scope_version":"linux-role-web-v17","units":["nginx.service","sshd.service","systemd-journald.service","dnf-makecache.timer"]}
```

The supplied collector rejects duplicate names, whitespace, slash characters, unsupported suffixes, more than 512 names, and an absent scope version. It does not expand globs or enumerate the manager. Include every exact policy unit assigned to the host. Configuration management should compare policy and target sets before rollout; the SPL additionally reports a policy unit absent from a fresh complete snapshot and scope-version disagreement.

## Step 2 — Deploy and verify the custom property collector

Place `scriptExample` at `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/TA-linux-systemd-unit-state/bin/collect_systemd_unit_state.py`, owned by the deployment administrator, executable, and not writable by the forwarder account or monitored applications. It invokes no shell. It finds `systemctl` under a fixed path, forces the C locale, applies a 20-second timeout per unit, and passes each validated unit as a separate argument. Review worst-case runtime: 512 serial 20-second timeouts are unacceptable. Start with a small critical inventory, measure latency, and either reduce targets or implement a separately reviewed bounded-concurrency collector while preserving output order independence and terminal completeness.

One invocation captures epoch, monotonic uptime, boot ID, random snapshot ID, target scope version, and target-file SHA-256. It calls `systemctl show` with an explicit property list. For each configured name it emits one `unit_state` object even when the manager says `LoadState=not-found`; that is a valid observed state, not collection absence. A nonzero query without `not-found` becomes `query_status=error`. Optional service-only properties remain null for other unit types. The script emits no command stderr in the event, avoiding uncontrolled journal/unit text; Splunk still documents scripted-input stderr in `splunkd.log` for scripts that write it.

After all names, the script emits one `snapshot_complete` object declaring `unit_count` and query errors. `collector_status=ok` means every configured unit produced either an ordinary property row or an explicit not-found row. Query errors make it `partial`. The SPL deduplicates transport copies by host/snapshot/type/unit and compares indexed unit rows with the declared count. A completion event arriving without every row becomes `index_incomplete`, even if the host-side collector declared success. Only status-ok count-complete snapshots supply unit state or restart deltas.

Configure `local/inputs.conf`:

```ini
[script://$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/TA-linux-systemd-unit-state/bin/collect_systemd_unit_state.py]
disabled = 0
interval = 60
index = os
source = linux_systemd_unit_state
sourcetype = linux:systemd:unit
```

Splunk documents that numeric interval is seconds, that the next interval follows completion, and that only one invocation per script runs per instance. Sixty seconds is therefore a target cadence. The expected daily event volume is `(units + 1) * 1,440` per host: 50 units produce 73,440 events/day/host. Measure serialized size, run time, indexing delay, forwarder CPU, and license volume on canaries.

Configure one JSON object per line on the parsing/search tiers:

```ini
[linux:systemd:unit]
SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false
LINE_BREAKER = ([\r\n]+)
TRUNCATE = 32768
TIME_PREFIX = "sample_epoch"\s*:\s*
TIME_FORMAT = %s
MAX_TIMESTAMP_LOOKAHEAD = 10
KV_MODE = json
```

Do not combine `KV_MODE=json` with `INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS=JSON`; Splunk documents that the fields would be extracted twice. The SPL includes `spath` for portable controls. Inspect effective settings with `splunk btool inputs list --debug` and `splunk btool props list linux:systemd:unit --debug`. Confirm one raw line per object, exact `host`, event time from `sample_epoch`, complete count, one scope hash/version, and no duplicate app assignment.

## Step 3 — Understand and schedule the SPL

Save the supplied search as `linux_systemd_unit_state_monitoring` and schedule it every five minutes. It searches from two hours ago through two minutes before dispatch. The closed two-minute delay prevents the newest snapshot completion from racing its unit rows; the two-hour history gives `streamstats` a prior complete sample and lets the search label a collector stale rather than immediately missing. Measure `_indextime-_time` and collector duration, then adjust bounds and controls together.

The first branch begins with policy, so a unit that produces no event remains present. The first event branch validates schema, identity, types, exact row count, and status for each snapshot. It sorts complete `unit_state` rows by host, unit, boot, and collector epoch before carrying the previous `NRestarts`; a changed boot ID cannot pair. A counter decrease yields no delta. It then retains only the newest valid complete snapshot per host.

The second event branch independently evaluates the newest collection attempt. If the terminal status is partial/configuration/prerequisite failure, or indexed count differs from declared count, that host's policy rows receive a collector finding and old unit properties are not interpreted as current. Embedded sample epoch, not search dispatch or `_indextime`, defines the ten-minute freshness test. Exactly 600 seconds is accepted; a future or older sample is stale. A host with no completion in two hours is missing.

After union, `stats` joins exact host/unit policy and observation while a synthetic collector row propagates host observer status. Duplicate policy keys and incomplete/expired policy fire before runtime interpretation. An observer is ready only when the newest attempt is status-ok, fresh, the exact unit exists in the latest valid complete snapshot, and its query is ok or explicit not-found. Scope disagreement is separate from state.

Desired lists are compared independently with observed load, active, sub, and unit-file states. This can intentionally produce multiple rows: `failed/failed` against `active/running` is both a high-level and substate mismatch, while `LoadState=not-found` can add load mismatch. Do not collapse those facts if different runbook actions use them. Boot/transition grace affects the four state comparisons only. `NeedDaemonReload=yes`, non-success checked service result, and a restart delta above policy remain explicit. Trigger on every row, route collector/policy failures to collection/configuration owners, and route unit findings by owner/tier. Throttle on `alert_key` for one schedule interval while retaining every dispatch result; do not throttle all findings for a host.

## Step 4 — Validate source truth, completeness, and controls

Run the collector interactively as the forwarder identity on one canary of every supported distribution and host role. Compare every populated field with same-time `systemctl show UNIT --all --no-pager --property=...` using the same property list. Check a running long-lived service, successful inactive oneshot, timer, socket, static unit, enabled unit, masked unit in a lab, failed service, template instance, alias, and a definitely nonexistent test name. Confirm not-found emits a unit row and does not make the snapshot partial. Confirm non-service rows leave service-only fields null rather than zero or success.

Verify complete-snapshot behavior. Record the target count, require exactly that many unique unit rows plus one completion, then duplicate a row, remove a row in an isolated fixture, duplicate the completion, and delay one unit beyond the search's latest boundary. Exact duplicates should deduplicate; a missing indexed row must make the latest attempt `index_incomplete`; old complete state must not generate runtime findings while that defect is current. Test configuration error, missing `systemctl`, command timeout, manager bus failure, target-file permission failure, and one per-unit query error. Each must be observer/query evidence, never fabricated `inactive` or zero restart state.

Run the exact positive and negative control narratives with fixed dispatch time. Assert exact finding names and counts. Add boundaries for collector ages 599, 600, and 601 seconds; boot/transition ages one second below, equal to, and above grace; restart deltas threshold-1, threshold, and threshold+1; counter decrease; changed boot ID; duplicate and expired policy; empty desired fields; scope-version mismatch; `NeedDaemonReload=yes`; result success, empty, exit-code, timeout, and signal; and each configured allowed state list.

Perform safe live state tests only on disposable units. Create a benign long-running test service and a successful oneshot, observe their documented state, then change only the test policy to prove desired-state handling. Under an approved lab change, stop or fail the test service, capture properties and journal, and verify findings and recovery. Test restart deltas with a bounded service designed to fail a known number of times and a conservative `StartLimit`; never induce flapping in a production dependency or weaken start limits to satisfy monitoring.

Validate application truth separately. For a service expected active, compare process, listening socket, local health endpoint, dependency, and transaction evidence. This UC can remain green while an active process serves errors. For timers, compare last/next trigger and triggered service result in a dedicated timer-execution control. For sockets, compare listener and activated service. Document those adjacent controls rather than extending `ActiveState` beyond its meaning.

This editorial review did not execute the collector, fixtures, SPL, alert, unit transitions, or a production rollout. Keep `status=draft`, omit Splunk-version validation claims, and record runtime results before promoting the content locally.

## Step 5 — Operationalize triage, evidence, and safe response

For collector missing/stale/incomplete findings, verify expected host identity, reachability, forwarder status/output queues, deployment assignment, effective input, script execution time, target file, manager namespace, and terminal row/count. Run the exact read-only collector or `systemctl show` as the configured identity. Do not call the unit down and do not remove expected inventory merely because observation failed.

For a state finding, first capture the raw unit row, policy revision, latest completion, prior complete sample, `systemctl show`, `systemctl status`, `systemctl cat`, relevant `journalctl -u UNIT --boot`, dependencies, recent package/configuration/change records, and application checks. Determine whether the unit is long-running, oneshot, activated, conditional, transient, templated, generated, or aliased before remediation. `ConditionResult=no`, a static unit file, or inactive/dead can be intended; `Result=exit-code`, `ExecMainStatus`, and journal identify execution failure but still need application context.

Never automatically run `systemctl restart`, `start`, `stop`, `enable`, `disable`, `mask`, `unmask`, `daemon-reload`, `reset-failed`, `kill`, or an arbitrary command from fields. Restart can destroy transient state, trigger dependency cascades, repeat destructive oneshots, violate quorum, or erase first-failure context. Unit-file changes and daemon reload affect configuration beyond one process. Follow the named owner's service-specific runbook, preserve evidence, check failover and dependencies, perform the approved action, then require a new complete snapshot plus application-level recovery evidence.

For a restart burst, compare boot and invocation identities, journal, `Restart=` policy, `RestartSec`, start-limit behavior, process exit status, watchdog/timeout, OOM, dependency, and deployment. A currently active service after six automatic restarts is recovered state with instability evidence, not a clean interval. Tune per-unit thresholds only after measuring legitimate lifecycle. Never sum `NRestarts` across hosts or graph the cumulative value as incident count.

Restrict dashboards and exports according to host/unit sensitivity; descriptions, paths, owners, failure modes, and service topology can reveal architecture. Retain evidence according to local operations policy. The 30-day cost entry is an estimate, not a mandated retention period. Review policy and collection scope after package, unit, role, host naming, systemd, hardening, forwarder, or application-lifecycle changes.

## Step 6 — Troubleshoot source-specific defects

- **No completion event:** inspect effective scripted input, executable/interpreter, target JSON, app permissions, script run time, forwarder `ExecProcessor` messages, output queues, and source routing. A script still running cannot satisfy a 60-second target cadence.
- **`configuration_error`:** validate UTF-8 JSON, schema/scope version, list shape, duplicates, unit suffixes, length limits, and file ownership. Do not fall back to enumerating currently loaded units.
- **`prerequisite_error`:** verify fixed command path and installed systemd client. A non-systemd host is outside scope; installing a binary alone does not create a host manager.
- **`query_status=error`:** run the exact `systemctl show` as the collector identity, verify local bus and namespace, timeout, manager responsiveness, and unit spelling. Preserve return code; do not translate the error to inactive.
- **`LoadState=not-found`:** verify exact canonical name, alias, template instance, package and generator output, manager scope, and desired inventory. If the unit was intentionally removed, change policy through governance; otherwise restore through the package/unit owner.
- **Inactive oneshots dominate:** correct per-unit desired active/sub state and check service result. Do not add a global `ActiveState!=active` exception.
- **Unit-file mismatches dominate:** review whether each unit is static, generated, transient, indirect, alias, template, runtime-enabled, or intentionally disabled. Enumerate valid states explicitly or use `ignore` with documented rationale; do not equate enablement and runtime.
- **Scope versions disagree:** compare lookup revision, host target file, SHA-256, configuration-management deployment, and app restart/refresh timing. Fix rollout; do not suppress absent units during prolonged drift.
- **Indexed count differs:** inspect event breaking/truncation, duplicate routes, queue loss, late indexing, host rewriting, and snapshot IDs. Widen delay only from measured latency; never change declared count in SPL or reuse partial state.
- **Restart delta is null:** there may be no prior complete sample, a changed boot, missing service property, counter decrease, or query gap. Preserve current value and source health; do not coalesce null to zero in evidence.
- **Unexpected state-change age:** compare monotonic properties with `/proc/uptime`, boot ID, manager behavior, and property availability on that systemd release. Keep null when unavailable and never mix monotonic microseconds with epoch seconds.
- **Stock `Unix:Service` disagrees:** compare collection time, exact unit identity, `service.sh` parsing, and field semantics. Use it as corroboration; it does not replace this desired-policy and complete-snapshot contract.

scriptExample:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Emit one complete snapshot of configured system-manager unit properties."""
import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import time
import uuid
from pathlib import Path

SCHEMA = 1
SAFE_PATH = "/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"
CONFIG = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "local" / "systemd-unit-targets.json"
UNIT_SUFFIXES = (".service", ".socket", ".timer", ".mount", ".automount", ".path", ".target", ".slice", ".scope", ".swap", ".device")
PROPERTIES = (
    "Id", "Names", "Description", "LoadState", "ActiveState", "FreezerState",
    "SubState", "UnitFileState", "UnitFilePreset", "NeedDaemonReload",
    "ConditionResult", "AssertResult", "StateChangeTimestampMonotonic",
    "ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic", "InactiveEnterTimestampMonotonic",
    "ActiveExitTimestampMonotonic", "InactiveExitTimestampMonotonic",
    "InvocationID", "FragmentPath", "SourcePath", "Type", "Result", "MainPID",
    "ExecMainCode", "ExecMainStatus", "NRestarts", "Restart",
)


def read_ascii(path, default="unknown"):
    try:
        return Path(path).read_text(encoding="ascii").strip()
    except OSError:
        return default


def integer(value):
    try:
        return int(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def emit(event):
    print(json.dumps(event, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True), flush=True)


def load_scope():
    raw = CONFIG.read_bytes()
    payload = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
    if payload.get("schema_version") != 1:
        raise ValueError("unsupported_scope_schema")
    scope_version = payload.get("scope_version")
    units = payload.get("units")
    if not isinstance(scope_version, str) or not scope_version or len(scope_version) > 160:
        raise ValueError("invalid_scope_version")
    if not isinstance(units, list) or len(units) > 512:
        raise ValueError("invalid_units")
    if len(units) != len(set(units)):
        raise ValueError("duplicate_units")
    for unit in units:
        if not isinstance(unit, str) or not unit or len(unit) > 255:
            raise ValueError("invalid_unit")
        if any(character.isspace() or character in "/\x00" for character in unit):
            raise ValueError("unsafe_unit")
        if not unit.endswith(UNIT_SUFFIXES):
            raise ValueError("unsupported_unit_type")
    return scope_version, units, hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()


def parse_properties(text):
    values = {}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        key, separator, value = line.partition("=")
        if separator:
            values[key] = value
    return values


def run_show(systemctl, unit):
    return subprocess.run(
        [systemctl, "show", unit, "--all", "--no-pager", "--property=" + ",".join(PROPERTIES)],
        check=False,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        encoding="utf-8",
        errors="replace",
        timeout=20,
        env={"PATH": SAFE_PATH, "LC_ALL": "C", "LANG": "C"},
    )


def base_event(snapshot_id, sample_epoch, sample_monotonic_usec, boot_id, boot_uptime_seconds, scope_version, scope_sha256):
    return {
        "collector_schema": SCHEMA,
        "snapshot_id": snapshot_id,
        "sample_epoch": sample_epoch,
        "sample_monotonic_usec": sample_monotonic_usec,
        "boot_id": boot_id,
        "boot_uptime_seconds": boot_uptime_seconds,
        "scope_version": scope_version,
        "scope_sha256": scope_sha256,
    }


def main():
    sample_epoch = int(time.time())
    uptime_text = read_ascii("/proc/uptime", "0").split()[0]
    boot_uptime_seconds = int(float(uptime_text))
    sample_monotonic_usec = int(float(uptime_text) * 1000000)
    boot_id = read_ascii("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id")
    snapshot_id = f"{boot_id}:{sample_epoch}:{uuid.uuid4()}"
    try:
        scope_version, units, scope_sha256 = load_scope()
    except (OSError, UnicodeError, ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
        event = base_event(snapshot_id, sample_epoch, sample_monotonic_usec, boot_id, boot_uptime_seconds, "unavailable", "unavailable")
        event.update(record_type="snapshot_complete", unit="__snapshot__", collector_status="configuration_error", collector_error_type=type(error).__name__, unit_count=0, query_error_count=0)
        emit(event)
        return
    base = base_event(snapshot_id, sample_epoch, sample_monotonic_usec, boot_id, boot_uptime_seconds, scope_version, scope_sha256)
    systemctl = shutil.which("systemctl", path=SAFE_PATH)
    if systemctl is None:
        event = dict(base)
        event.update(record_type="snapshot_complete", unit="__snapshot__", collector_status="prerequisite_error", collector_error_type="systemctl_unavailable", unit_count=0, query_error_count=0)
        emit(event)
        return
    query_errors = 0
    for requested_unit in units:
        event = dict(base)
        event.update(record_type="unit_state", unit=requested_unit)
        try:
            result = run_show(systemctl, requested_unit)
            properties = parse_properties(result.stdout)
            load_state = properties.get("LoadState")
            query_status = "ok" if result.returncode == 0 else ("not_found" if load_state == "not-found" else "error")
            if query_status == "error":
                query_errors += 1
            event.update(
                query_status=query_status,
                query_return_code=result.returncode,
                returned_unit=properties.get("Id"),
                unit_names=properties.get("Names"),
                unit_description=properties.get("Description"),
                load_state=load_state,
                active_state=properties.get("ActiveState"),
                sub_state=properties.get("SubState"),
                freezer_state=properties.get("FreezerState"),
                unit_file_state=properties.get("UnitFileState"),
                unit_file_preset=properties.get("UnitFilePreset"),
                need_daemon_reload=properties.get("NeedDaemonReload"),
                condition_result=properties.get("ConditionResult"),
                assert_result=properties.get("AssertResult"),
                state_change_monotonic_usec=integer(properties.get("StateChangeTimestampMonotonic")),
                active_enter_monotonic_usec=integer(properties.get("ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic")),
                inactive_enter_monotonic_usec=integer(properties.get("InactiveEnterTimestampMonotonic")),
                active_exit_monotonic_usec=integer(properties.get("ActiveExitTimestampMonotonic")),
                inactive_exit_monotonic_usec=integer(properties.get("InactiveExitTimestampMonotonic")),
                invocation_id=properties.get("InvocationID"),
                fragment_path=properties.get("FragmentPath"),
                source_path=properties.get("SourcePath"),
                service_type=properties.get("Type"),
                service_result=properties.get("Result"),
                main_pid=integer(properties.get("MainPID")),
                exec_main_code=integer(properties.get("ExecMainCode")),
                exec_main_status=integer(properties.get("ExecMainStatus")),
                n_restarts=integer(properties.get("NRestarts")),
                restart_policy=properties.get("Restart"),
            )
        except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as error:
            query_errors += 1
            event.update(query_status="error", query_return_code=None, query_error_type=type(error).__name__)
        emit(event)
    event = dict(base)
    event.update(record_type="snapshot_complete", unit="__snapshot__", collector_status="ok" if query_errors == 0 else "partial", unit_count=len(units), query_error_count=query_errors)
    emit(event)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
